newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cuts petrol tax by six percent.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cuts petrol tax by six percent.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Friday it had cut tax on petrol by about six percent to increase the income of petrol traders and producers.

"Tax on a litre of unleaded petrol was reduced to 38.37 tolars from 40.70 tolars to increase the income of petrol firms that was lower due to the recent rise in crude oil prices," Davor Valentincic, state secretary for trade, told Reuters.
He said petrol prices would remain unchanged although petrol firms had asked for a price increase of 11 to 20 percent. Currently the price of a litre of unleaded petrol is 76.2 tolars ($0.6).

Valentincic also said the government was likely to raise tax on petrol next year to replace a fall in income from customs tax from January, due to trade agreements with the European Union and the Central European free trade area.
"I expect petrol prices will next year be increased by at least 10 percent due to higher tax," Valentincic said.
This year petrol prices were raised twice, altogether by about nine percent.
